goal.objective:
Implement `src/intervals.js`, a set algebra over half-open integer intervals. An interval is a two-element array `[start, end)` of safe integers that covers every integer x with `start <= x < end`. An interval list is normalised when it is sorted by start, contains no empty interval, and no two of its members overlap or touch: `[1, 3)` and `[3, 5)` touch and must coalesce into `[1, 5)`, while `[1, 3)` and `[4, 5)` must stay apart.

Export five functions. `normalize(intervals)` returns the normalised form of one list. `merge(a, b)` returns the normalised union of two lists. `intersect(a, b)` returns the normalised intersection; touching intervals share no integer, so `[1, 3)` against `[3, 5)` yields an empty list. `subtract(a, b)` returns the normalised relative complement `a \ b`. `coverage(intervals)` returns how many integers the list covers, counting an integer covered by several intervals once.

Every function validates both of its interval-list arguments before doing any work, and inputs may be adversarial: unsorted, duplicated, nested, negative, empty (`start === end`, which normalisation drops), or spanning a large range. A value that is not an array raises `TypeError` with message `interval list must be an array`. A member that is not a two-element array raises `TypeError` with message `interval must be a two-element array`. A bound that is not a safe integer — a float, a numeric string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, or a value beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — raises `TypeError` with message `interval bounds must be safe integers`. An interval whose start exceeds its end raises `RangeError` with message `interval start must not exceed end`.

No function may mutate its arguments or return arrays that alias them; every returned interval is freshly allocated. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

1: import { test } from 'node:test';
2: import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

4: import { coverage, intersect, merge, normalize, subtract } from '../src/intervals.js';

6: /** Lower bound of the universe used by the model-based checks. */
7: const LO = -40;
8: /** Upper bound (exclusive) of the universe used by the model-based checks. */
9: const HI = 40;
10: 
11: /**
12:  * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG.
13:  * @param {number} seed Initial state.
14:  * @returns {() => number} Generator returning floats in [0, 1).
15:  */
16: function mulberry32(seed) {
17:   let a = seed >>> 0;
18:   return () => {
19:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
20:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
21:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
22:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
23:   };
24: }
25: 
26: /**
27:  * Rasterises an interval list over the model universe.
28:  * @param {Array<[number, number]>} list Interval list.
29:  * @returns {Uint8Array} One byte per integer in [LO, HI).
30:  */
31: function raster(list) {
32:   const bits = new Uint8Array(HI - LO);
33:   for (const [start, end] of list) {
34:     for (let x = Math.max(start, LO); x < Math.min(end, HI); x += 1) bits[x - LO] = 1;
35:   }
36:   return bits;
37: }
38: 
39: /**
40:  * Converts a raster back into a normalised interval list.
41:  * @param {Uint8Array} bits Raster.
42:  * @returns {Array<[number, number]>} Normalised list.
43:  */
44: function unraster(bits) {
45:   const out = [];
46:   let run = -1;
47:   for (let i = 0; i <= bits.length; i += 1) {
48:     const on = i < bits.length && bits[i] === 1;
49:     if (on && run < 0) run = i;
50:     if (!on && run >= 0) {
51:       out.push([run + LO, i + LO]);
52:       run = -1;
53:     }
54:   }
55:   return out;
56: }
57: 
58: /**
59:  * Asserts that a list is normalised: sorted, non-empty, disjoint, non-touching.
60:  * @param {Array<[number, number]>} list List under test.
61:  * @param {string} label Assertion label.
62:  * @returns {void}
63:  */
64: function assertNormalised(list, label) {
65:   for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i += 1) {
66:     assert.ok(list[i][0] < list[i][1], `${label}: empty interval at ${i}`);
67:     if (i > 0) assert.ok(list[i - 1][1] < list[i][0], `${label}: not disjoint at ${i}`);
68:   }
69: }
70: 
71: /**
72:  * Builds a random interval list.
73:  * @param {() => number} rnd Generator.
74:  * @param {number} count How many intervals.
75:  * @returns {Array<[number, number]>} Random intervals, possibly empty ones.
76:  */
77: function randomList(rnd, count) {
78:   const out = [];
79:   for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
80:     const start = LO + Math.floor(rnd() * (HI - LO - 9));
81:     const width = Math.floor(rnd() * 9);
82:     out.push([start, start + width]);
83:   }
84:   return out;
85: }

"prompt": "Implement `src/intervals.js`, a set algebra over half-open integer intervals. An interval is a two-element array `[start, end)` of safe integers that covers every integer x with `start <= x < end`. An interval list is normalised when it is sorted by start, contains no empty interval, and no two of its members overlap or touch: `[1, 3)` and `[3, 5)` touch and must coalesce into `[1, 5)`, while `[1, 3)` and `[4, 5)` must stay apart.

Export five functions. `normalize(intervals)` returns the normalised form of one list. `merge(a, b)` returns the normalised union of two lists. `intersect(a, b)` returns the normalised intersection; touching intervals share no integer, so `[1, 3)` against `[3, 5)` yields an empty list. `subtract(a, b)` returns the normalised relative complement `a \ b`. `coverage(intervals)` returns how many integers the list covers, counting an integer covered by several intervals once.

Every function validates both of its interval-list arguments before doing any work, and inputs may be adversarial: unsorted, duplicated, nested, negative, empty (`start === end`, which normalisation drops), or spanning a large range. A value that is not an array raises `TypeError` with message `interval list must be an array`. A member that is not a two-element array raises `TypeError` with message `interval must be a two-element array`. A bound that is not a safe integer — a float, a numeric string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, or a value beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — raises `TypeError` with message `interval bounds must be safe integers`. An interval whose start exceeds its end raises `RangeError` with message `interval start must not exceed end`.

No function may mutate its arguments or return arrays that alias them; every returned interval is freshly allocated. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`.",

goal.objective:
Implement `src/intervals.js`, a set algebra over half-open integer intervals. An interval is a two-element array `[start, end)` of safe integers that covers every integer x with `start <= x < end`. An interval list is normalised when it is sorted by start, contains no empty interval, and no two of its members overlap or touch: `[1, 3)` and `[3, 5)` touch and must coalesce into `[1, 5)`, while `[1, 3)` and `[4, 5)` must stay apart.

Export five functions. `normalize(intervals)` returns the normalised form of one list. `merge(a, b)` returns the normalised union of two lists. `intersect(a, b)` returns the normalised intersection; touching intervals share no integer, so `[1, 3)` against `[3, 5)` yields an empty list. `subtract(a, b)` returns the normalised relative complement `a \ b`. `coverage(intervals)` returns how many integers the list covers, counting an integer covered by several intervals once.

Every function validates both of its interval-list arguments before doing any work, and inputs may be adversarial: unsorted, duplicated, nested, negative, empty (`start === end`, which normalisation drops), or spanning a large range. A value that is not an array raises `TypeError` with message `interval list must be an array`. A member that is not a two-element array raises `TypeError` with message `interval must be a two-element array`. A bound that is not a safe integer — a float, a numeric string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, or a value beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — raises `TypeError` with message `interval bounds must be safe integers`. An interval whose start exceeds its end raises `RangeError` with message `interval start must not exceed end`.

No function may mutate its arguments or return arrays that alias them; every returned interval is freshly allocated. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
